nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of the unnormalized bound, if $|\lambda_j - \lambda_{i_0}| \le D$ for every $j$, then the Rayleigh quotient of $x = T^k v_0$ satisfies $|\langle x, Tx\rangle/\|x\|^2 - \lambda_{i_0}| \le D\rho^{2k}(\|v_0\|/|c|)^2$.
nodes.title: The power-iteration eigenvalue estimate converges twice as fast

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of the unnormalized bound, the power iterates $v_k = T^k v_0 / \|T^k v_0\|$ satisfy $\|v_k - s_k q\| \le 2\rho^k \|v_0\|/|c|$ for some sign $s_k = \pm 1$.
nodes.title: Power iteration converges to the dominant eigenvector up to sign

nodes.summary: If $T$ is symmetric and $Tq = \lambda q$, then for every $v$, $\langle v, Tv\rangle - \lambda\|v\|^2 = \langle v - q, (T - \lambda)(v - q)\rangle$. Hence the Rayleigh quotient $r(v) = \langle v, Tv\rangle/\|v\|^2$ satisfies $r(v) - \lambda = O(\|v - q\|^2)$: it is a quadratically accurate estimate of the eigenvalue.
nodes.title: Quadratic accuracy of the Rayleigh quotient

nodes.summary: If $(b_j)$ is an orthonormal basis of a real inner product space with $T b_j = \lambda_j b_j$, then $\langle b_j, T^k v\rangle = \lambda_j^k \langle b_j, v\rangle$ for every $v$ and $k$.

nodes.summary: If $\|q\| = 1$, then $\| y/\|y\| - q\| \le 2\|y - q\|$ for every $y$ (with $0/0 = 0$).
